deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page): X is a topological space and F ⊂ P(X) is a family of subsets. a) and b) make F a Boolean algebra: stable under finite unions and intersections, and under complements. c) makes F stable under closure; given a), this is equivalent to stability under interior. This page adds two 'tameness' axioms.

(d) For every A ∈ F, the interior of A (read: relative to Ā) is dense in Ā. Equivalently, Ā − int_Ā(A) is rare (closed and nowhere dense) in Ā, and hence rare in X, since Ā is closed. So every definable set contains a dense open subset of its closure. This is the topological shadow of the o-minimal frontier inequality dim(Ā−A) < dim A.

(e) A descending chain condition. There is no infinite strictly decreasing chain A1 ⊃ A2 ⊃ … of closed sets of F with each A_{n+1} rare in A_n. Any such chain reaches ∅. This is a 'finite dimension' axiom, with dimension measured by nowhere-density, in the spirit of Krull dimension or Noetherian induction.

NB. The Boolean algebra generated by a family 𝔉 is the set of finite unions of sets A ∩ ∁B with A, B ∈ 𝔉. This tacitly requires 𝔉 to be a lattice containing ∅ and X; the next page studies exactly this.

Proposition. If F satisfies a)–e), then F is the Boolean algebra generated by its closed members (call that algebra F').

Proof.
- Write Ā = Å ∪ bA, where bA is the boundary. Then A = Å ∪ (A ∩ bA).
- Å = ∁(closure of ∁A) lies in F', using b) and c).
- It remains to show A ∩ bA ∈ F'.
- By d), bA is rare in X. Indeed, an open set V ⊂ bA would meet the dense relatively open part of Ā lying in A in a nonempty open set of X contained in A, hence in Å. That is impossible.
- Set X1 = bA. It is closed and lies in F. Let F1 be the trace of F on X1 and A1 = A ∩ X1. The axioms pass to F1.
- Closed members of F1 are closed in X and belong to F. So A1 ∈ F'1 implies A1 ∈ F', and then A ∈ F'.
- Iterating gives a chain X = X0 ⊃ X1 ⊃ … of closed F-sets, each rare in the previous one.
- By e), X_n = ∅ for some n. Then A_n = ∅ ∈ F'_n, and the induction unwinds.

Purpose. This is an axiomatic 'constructibility' theorem for a putative tame topology. Every definable set is a Boolean combination of closed definable sets, i.e. a finite union of locally closed ones. It is the analogue of EGA's constructible sets in Noetherian spaces, proved by a rarity-based Noetherian induction.
errors: The transcription of d) ('l'intérieur [de A] est dense dans Ā') cannot mean the interior in X: a point of R would violate it. It must be the interior relative to Ā (equivalently Ā − int_Ā A rare in Ā). The 'i.e. son complémentaire rare dans Ā' supports this reading.

The NB is stated for an arbitrary 𝔉 ⊂ P(X). It is only correct if 𝔉 is stable under finite unions and intersections and contains ∅ and X. In general one needs finite unions of finite intersections of sets of 𝔉 and their complements. The following page takes up this lattice condition.
'Å ∈ F' grâce à b)' really uses both b) (complement) and c) (closure). A minor citation slip.
The induction step tacitly uses that F1 = F|X1 again satisfies a)–e), and that X1 ∈ F (by c)). Both are true but unstated.

ideas.what: Axiom (d): every definable set contains a dense relatively open subset of its closure, so frontiers and boundaries are rare.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition / small boundaries in o-minimal and tame topology (dim(Ā−A) < dim A)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86); topological axiomatics: Pillay, 'First order topological structures' (1987), Mathews (1995)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic mention of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5); no axioms given there

ideas.what: Axiom (e): DCC on chains of closed definable sets each nowhere dense in the previous one.
ideas.modern_name: Finite (topological) dimension / Noetherian-type induction on rarity; cf. dimension via nowhere density in topological first-order structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pillay (1987); Mathews; also Krull-dimension-style arguments in EGA
ideas.where_published: Analogous Noetherian induction in EGA 0_III §9 (constructible sets); this precise rare-chain axiom not known to be published

ideas.what: Proposition: under a)–e), the Boolean algebra F is generated by its closed members, i.e. every definable set is a finite union of locally closed definable sets.
ideas.modern_name: Constructibility of definable sets (finite union of locally closed definable sets); analogue of EGA constructible sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal cell decomposition (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn 1986; van den Dries 1998); EGA 0_III 9.1 for Noetherian spaces (Grothendieck–Dieudonné)

ideas.what: NB on the Boolean algebra generated by a family (finite unions of A∩∁B).
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra generated by a lattice of sets

missed.claim: In 1974 Grothendieck had a purely topological axiomatization of a 'tame' family of sets. It comprises Boolean algebra, closure-stability, dense relative interior and a DCC on rare chains. He proved that such a family is generated by its closed members, a precursor of Pillay-style 'first-order topological structures' and of the o-minimal fact that definable sets are finite unions of locally closed ones. This predates the o-minimality literature by about a decade.
missed.quote: Prop Si F satisfait a) à e), alors F est "engendré" par l'ensemble des parties fermées ∈ F.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' had concrete axioms close to those of later axiomatic tame topology, not just the vague programme of the Esquisse. This is relevant for crediting and for comparing his axioms (rarity-based, no dimension function) with Pillay's and Mathews'.

missed.claim: The proof is a Noetherian induction in which 'nowhere dense closed subset' replaces 'proper closed subset'. This explicitly transplants EGA-style constructibility to tame topology.
missed.quote: On construit ainsi de proche en proche X0 = X ⊃ X1 ⊃ ... avec X_{n+1} rare dans X_n ... Or ∃n tel que X_n = ∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean bridge between scheme-theoretic constructible sets and o-minimal/definable topology. The later literature developed these largely independently.

deep.surprise_reason: The result itself is easy and now standard in o-minimal settings. Still, it is a concrete 1974 axiomatic attempt at tame topology with a correct proof, anticipating Pillay-style axioms, and it is not reflected in the published record beyond the Esquisse's programmatic remarks.
transcription_corrections: 'Ā = Å ∪ bÅ' should read 'Ā = Å ∪ bA' (bA = boundary of A). Likewise 'X remplacé par bÅ = X1' should be 'bA = X1'.
d) should read: 'l'intérieur [de A relatif à Ā] est dense dans Ā, i.e. son complémentaire [dans Ā] est rare dans Ā (et a fortiori dans X)'.
'On prend[?] d'après d)' is probably 'Or, d'après d), X1 est rare dans X'.
'Si 𝔉 satisfait a) à e)[?]': the image indeed reads 'a) à e)' (or 'à ...'), consistent with the proof using c), d), e).
'telles que si A_n ∈ F'_n ⇒ A ∈ F'' should read 'telles que A_n ∈ F'_n ⇒ A ∈ F''.
